subject: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification — network details & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <t.alvarez@zenmed.com>, Lina Torres <lina.torres@zenmed.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification — network details & next steps

Hi Tom / Lina —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same notes and clear next steps. If I missed anything, please correct me.

Call recap (high level):
- Goal: deploy Redwood Private (VPC) behind ZenMed networking for PII workflows; run production inference with SLOs and predictable unit economics.
- Target performance/throughput: steady-state 500 qps (text generation), burst to 1k qps for short windows.
- Concurrency: ~50 concurrent requests for the main inference endpoint.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 150ms for non-streaming, p99 tail ideally < 400ms. For streaming (server-side chunked responses) we need sub-100ms per chunk to keep UX smooth.
- Protocols: HTTP/1.1 & HTTP/2 supported; WebSocket not required at launch but helpful long-term.

Network qualification items we need from ZenMed to validate feasibility:
1) Preferred private connectivity option: VNet peering (ExpressRoute) or IPsec VPN? Any constraints around peering?
2) High-level network path: cloud region (you mentioned Azure us-east-2), subnet CIDR(s) for any staging/test VPC, NAT/firewall hops, and whether there is a reverse proxy or egress proxy for outbound traffic.
3) Egress constraints and bandwidth limits (we'll need to estimate token egress and model artifacts transfer during updates).
4) Expected internal latency budget (your internal SLA between application and inference nodes) — this helps size node placement relative to app tier.
5) Any port/IP whitelisting process, MTU settings, or VPN/device vendor specifics we should plan for.

Attachments: I attached our Redwood Private network requirements and a short checklist (redwood-private-vpc-reqs.pdf).

Next steps / asks:
- Can you share a network diagram and traffic estimates (if available) — ZenMed diagram + traffic csv would be ideal.
- Please confirm whether ExpressRoute + VNet peering is available, or whether we'll need to plan for IPsec VPN.
- If acceptable, let's schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive (Jordan + infra) next week to walk the network team through the test plan and perf-validation.

Proposed times: Tue/Wed next week 10:00–12:00 PT or 14:00–16:00 PT.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call today if any of this needs clarifying.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0133

Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-reqs.pdf

From: Tom Alvarez <t.alvarez@zenmed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lina Torres <lina.torres@zenmed.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification — network details & next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary and the deck. Good talk. A few notes from our side:

Current infra:
- We run in Azure (primary region us-east-2) using ExpressRoute to our on-prem DC; typical workloads live in a set of VNets with service endpoints.
- For connectivity options to vendors we prefer VNet peering when possible (lower latency) but we can stand up an IPsec site-to-site tunnel for initial testing if peering is not possible from vendor side.

Network details (high level):
- Firewall/NAT: outbound egress goes through an Azure NAT gateway; there is a perimeter firewall for inbound to certain subnets (we can open ports as needed with a change request).
- Internal latency budget: application tier-to-inference should target < 50ms RTT internal to region; cross-region calls are possible but will add ~60–120ms additional.
- Throughput/egress: we can support sustained 500 qps for testing; full production will need a capacity exercise but traffic estimates are attached.

I attached: zenmed-network-diagram.pdf and zenmed-traffic-estimates.csv.

Operational constraints:
- We have a centralized egress proxy for some services — need to confirm if Redwood requires direct outbound to public IPs for updates/artifact pulls or if proxying is acceptable.
- MTU: default 1500; some VPN endpoints require 1400 — we'll confirm.

Next steps from our side:
- Lina (cc'd) is our network lead and will coordinate firewall rules and peering approvals.
- We can provide a staging VNet with restricted access for perf tests if Redwood signs the network access form.

Availability for deep-dive: Wed Mar 17 11:00–12:00 ET or Thu Mar 18 09:00–11:00 ET. Let me know which works.

Thanks,
Tom Alvarez
Director, Infrastructure | ZenMed
t.alvarez@zenmed.com | +1 (617) 555-0099

Attachments: zenmed-network-diagram.pdf, zenmed-traffic-estimates.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <t.alvarez@zenmed.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Lina Torres <lina.torres@zenmed.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification — network details & next steps

Tom / Lina —

Appreciate the diagram and the traffic csv — exactly what we needed. Quick responses inline and a short checklist to keep momentum: 

- VNet peering preferred — great. We'll prioritize peering during the pilot; fallback to IPsec for the initial perf window if peering approvals take longer.
- Internal latency budget noted (app <-> inference < 50ms). We'll plan to place inference nodes in us-east-2 and run region-local synthetic tests to validate.
- Egress/proxy: we can work with your egress proxy (we've done this with other customers) but we will need a list of outbound URLs/IPs and ports to allow (we'll provide a short whitelist).
- MTU: please confirm if your VPN endpoints require 1400 for site-to-site; otherwise we'll assume 1500.

Requested artifacts from ZenMed to proceed with the pilot:
1) Staging VNet access (CIDR + contact) or a peering request template.
2) Confirmation on whether a NAT egress proxy will be used and a point of contact for proxy configuration.
3) Any network ACLs/firewall approval lead for change requests.

I'll have Jordan coordinate the technical deep-dive. Proposed time: Thu Mar 18 09:00–10:00 ET (your window) works for Jordan and Aditya on our side — can you confirm?

Once we have staging access we'll run a quick 3-step validation:
A) small synthetic latency tests (p95/p99 guidance), B) throughput soak to your 500 qps target for 30 minutes, C) streaming chunk timing tests for UX validation.

I'll attach a short next-steps doc and the test plan separately (redwood-private-vpc-reqs.pdf included earlier).

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-reqs.pdf

From: Tom Alvarez <t.alvarez@zenmed.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0400

Marissa / Jordan —

Confirming Thu Mar 18 09:00–10:00 ET for the technical deep-dive. Lina will send a calendar invite and the peering request template after this note.

Immediate items we can share ahead of the meeting:
- Staging VNet CIDR: 10.42.0.0/16 (we'll provide IAM contact in the invite)
- We can open the NAT gateway egress for your test IPs during the window; please provide the egress IPs you will originate from.
- Proxy: we can support outbound through the egress proxy; Lina will confirm proxy host/port and auth requirements.

We'll also prepare a short list of firewall changes (ports and IPs) and any compliance items (SOC 2 evidence) that your team needs for the pilot.

See you Thursday — invite coming from Lina.

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Infrastructure | ZenMed
